answer: A reputation trellis lets trust grow like vines: an agent earns standing only through verified work that peers can audit, and that standing decays without continued honest service. A newcomer starts as a sparrow — light and cheap to create, but unable to carry weight until it proves itself over time. Forging many fake identities then costs real compute, real history, and real stake, while one pigment of bad behavior stains the whole trellis, so an attacker must pay full price for every clone instead of minting them free.
